source.check: deemed re-elected: 'No nomination was received for Errigal, Foremass, Newtownsaville, and Fivemiletown, and the respective sitting members, Patrick M'Kelvey, John Kelly, John Monaghan (Nationalists), and Andrew Crawford (Unionist), were returned' (Irish News, 6 May 1936, p. 7)

note: Triennial election of the rural district councillors. Nominations were received on 5 May 1936. Eleven divisions were filled unopposed; no nominations were received in Errigal, Fivemiletown, Foremass and Newtownsaville, whose sitting members were deemed re-elected (Irish News, 6 May 1936, p. 7), and Cullamore was contested between the sitting member, Mr. James E. Hackett, and Mr. James Gormley, another Nationalist (Belfast News-Letter, 6 May 1936, p. 9). The Cullamore result has not been found, so Cullamore is not recorded. Filed on 1936-06-03, the Tyrone polling day (previously filed under 1936-05-28, 6 Nov 2026). No nomination; the sitting member, named in the election's report, was deemed re-elected. Deemed re-elected (no nomination).
